meta.description: Multi-pathogen profile definitions for concurrent simulation
meta.notes: Each pathogen runs as an independent instance with separate mass pools per room. Profiles can be activated at initiation or introduced mid-cruise via 'introduction_epoch'.

pathogens.name: Norwalk Virus (Norovirus GII.4)

incubation.notes: Pooled norovirus GII: mu 0.182, sigma 0.445 (median 1.2 d, GSD 1.56, 95% 0.5-2.9 d) from Lee et al. 2013 via docs/ctb_incubation_spec.md - GII rather than the GI the pathogen_id implies, because this profile's genotypes are GII.4/GII.17/GII.2, and the spec finds no genotype-specific fits within GII. Dose term dose_shift 0.12 / floor 0.3 from the spec. dose_reference_log10 is this profile's own beta-Poisson N50 (16871 particles, alpha 0.111 / beta 32.81), not the spec's 18 RT-PCR units: acquired_particles is in model units, so referencing the literature assay unit would put every simulated host on the dose floor and turn a conditioning term into a constant. Consequence: a typical (near-ID50) host presents at the literature median, and the dose effect is anchored in direction but not calibrated in magnitude. host_factors omitted deliberately: the spec finds no literature support for a frailty effect on incubation, so it stays a sensitivity arm.

strain_evolution.notes: Rates from docs/paper3/variant_surveillance_spec.md §1.3. superinfection_susceptibility and recombination_rate are placeholders pending a literature anchor (docs/paper3/variant_surveillance_plan.md §7). immune_waning: refractory_days 56 and half_life_days 1095 are anchored on homotypic challenge protection lasting at least months and modelled immunity duration of 4.1-8.7 years (Simmons et al., Emerg Infect Dis 2013); the homotypic HR 0.39 of Ford-Siltz et al. (Clin Infect Dis 2020) is a multi-year hazard ratio, not a per-epoch susceptibility. Both are sensitivity axes. refractory_protection is applied as a per-epoch hazard reduction, so any value below 1.0 leaks at that rate every hour: 1.0 makes within-window re-infection escape-only, which is the intended contract.

sequencing_assay.notes: Assay design from docs/paper3/variant_surveillance_spec.md §2.1. read_accuracy is per-read consensus accuracy for this amplicon; read depth and the reporting floor are operator dials set at run time, not pathogen properties.

pathogens.presymptomatic_shedding_notes: Atmar et al., Emerg Infect Dis 2008: virus was first detected in stool at a median approximately 36 hours post-challenge, essentially concurrent with symptom onset; 0.5 days is the generous presymptomatic window.

pathogens.name: SARS-CoV-2 (Respiratory)

incubation.notes: SARS-CoV-2 ancestral: mu 1.758, sigma 0.450 (median 5.8 d, GSD 1.57, 95% 2.3-14.6 d) from Wei et al. 2021 via docs/ctb_incubation_spec.md. Later lineages incubate faster (Omicron median 3.5 d, mu 1.253 / sigma 0.400): set median_days per scenario rather than treating 5.8 as current. Dose term dose_shift 0.15 / floor 0.3 from the spec, referenced to this profile's own beta-Poisson N50 (2670 particles, alpha 0.18 / beta 58) rather than the spec's TCID50 figure, for the model-unit reason given on norwalk_gi.

strain_evolution.notes: Rates from docs/paper3/variant_surveillance_spec.md §1.3. superinfection_susceptibility and recombination_rate are placeholders pending a literature anchor (docs/paper3/variant_surveillance_plan.md §7). immune_waning: refractory_days 90 follows the 90-day reinfection convention; half_life_days 180 reflects rapid waning of protection against infection, with a small residual. Sensitivity axis. refractory_protection is applied as a per-epoch hazard reduction, so any value below 1.0 leaks at that rate every hour: 1.0 makes within-window re-infection escape-only, which is the intended contract.

sequencing_assay.notes: Assay design from docs/paper3/variant_surveillance_spec.md §2.1. read_accuracy is per-read consensus accuracy for this amplicon; read depth and the reporting floor are operator dials set at run time, not pathogen properties.

pathogens.presymptomatic_shedding_notes: He et al., Nat Med 2020: infectiousness begins approximately 2.3 days before symptom onset; 2.0 days is the profile window.

pathogens.name: Influenza A (pooled)
pathogens.notes: Pooled influenza A: no subtype-specific biology. The Edison bundle's H1N1/H3N2 strain table, base_susceptibility 0.65, dose_adjustment, surface_deposition_fraction and share-valued transmission_route_weights are deliberately not carried over; see docs/parameter_provenance_register.md section 3.3 for why each is refused, and docs/proposals/influenza_arm_activation_plan.md for the activation sequence. Scored rungs are MAARI and NAT-confirmed infection, kept separate.
pathogens.presymptomatic_shedding_notes: Ip et al., Clin Infect Dis 2017: shedding begins approximately 1 day before symptom onset; 1.0 day is the profile window.
pathogens.environmental_release_notes: Level, not shape. Emission is 10^(curve - this value) per day, converted to the epoch by SimClock, so 0.82 sets the symptomatic peak (curve 7.2) to 10^6.38 = 2.4e6 copies per day, which is Yan 2018 (EMIT, PNAS 115:1081, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1716561115) exhaled geometric means 3.8e4 fine + 1.2e4 coarse copies per 30-min sample extrapolated to 24 h. Grade C: the measurement is exhaled breath in a clinical facility, and Yan finds exhaled load uncorrelated with NP swab load, so the nasal-indexed curve supplies only the temporal shape while the level is pinned to a measured exhaled rate. Excludes hand contamination and large-droplet spray, so it is a lower bound on total release. Declared, and selected against no anchor.
pathogens.airborne_emission_notes: Fine (<=5 um) share of exhaled emission, 3.8e4 / (3.8e4 + 1.2e4) = 0.76 from the same Yan 2018 paired measurement. The coarse remainder deposits near the source, which is what the fomite route draws on. Replaces the Edison bundle's surface_deposition_fraction 1e-3, which was the deprecated alias of this key with no stated referent.

severity_model.evidence_grade: B for the two rungs Carrat measures, P for the splits inside them
severity_model.notes: Carrat 2008 (DOI 10.1093/aje/kwm375) fixes two rungs: any symptoms 66.9% of infections, so asymptomatic + subclinical = 0.331; lower-respiratory symptoms 21.0% of infections, read as moderate or worse. Mild = 0.669 - 0.210 = 0.459 is then implied. The two splits inside those rungs (asymptomatic vs subclinical 0.200/0.131, moderate vs severe_critical 0.200/0.010) are declared, not measured, and are swept. No value here was chosen against Ward 2010 or Millman 2015.

active_screening.notes: Off by default, which makes the arm's baseline passive infirmary ascertainment. Ward 2010's research testing of a whole voyage is represented by enabling this and raising selection_probability_per_day, not by widening the sampling vector below: a case-finding campaign reaches symptomatic hosts who never presented, and passive sampling cannot.

observation_model.notes: Every number here is declared and swept, because the arm's candidate anchors are themselves observation-layer quantities: setting these to reproduce Ward's 0.7% presenting or Millman's 3.7%/6.2% MAARI would make those anchors unfalsifiable. Recorded for comparison rather than calibration: these values imply a pre-recognition medically-attended fraction near 0.16 per infection against the roughly 0.08 Ward measures on one voyage (0.7% presenting against 8.9% NAT-confirmed), so the arm starts about 2x too visible and closing that is the sweep's job. assay_sensitivity 0.95 is RT-PCR on an adequate NP specimen (Grade C), kept separate from the sampling vector so that detection-technology scenarios move sensitivity without moving clinical behaviour.

incubation.notes: Human influenza A: mu 0.336, sigma 0.412 (median 1.4 d, GSD 1.51) from Lessler et al. 2009 via docs/ctb_incubation_spec.md, truncated 0.5-7.0 d to match the tng_shipboard_influenza analogue that already carries this same kernel as a shape. Dose terms dose_shift 0.10 / floor 0.4 from the spec. dose_reference_log10 0.59 is this profile's own exponential-model N50 (ln(2)/k = 0.693/0.18 = 3.85 particles), the exponential analogue of the beta-Poisson N50 convention documented on norwalk_gi in active_profiles.json: acquired_particles is in model units, so referencing a literature TCID50 or EID50 figure would put every simulated host on the dose floor and turn a conditioning term into a constant. Consequence: a near-ID50 host presents at the literature median, and the dose effect is anchored in direction but not calibrated in magnitude. host_factors omitted, as on the shipped profiles.

pathogens.shedding_duration_notes: Separated from recovery_day 5 so clinical resolution does not end shedding, the defect fixed for norovirus in #43. Seven days spans Carrat 2008's reported shedding through about day 5 plus Ip 2017's presymptomatic day; the 15-value curve's tail beyond it contributes under 1% of the linear-scale integral.
pathogens.base_susceptibility_notes: Deliberately 1.0, not the Edison bundle's 0.65. Prior immunity is a per-season, subtype- and age-conditioned scenario input: on Ward's single voyage pdm09 ran at RR 17.4 in children 3-6 with zero cases over 65 while H3N2 was flat across every age band, so no scalar represents it. It is declared on the manifest and swept, never fitted here.

sequencing_assay.notes: Assay design from docs/paper3/variant_surveillance_spec.md §2.1. read_accuracy is per-read consensus accuracy for this amplicon; read depth and the reporting floor are operator dials set at run time, not pathogen properties.
